why:
The line discount, and the two things about it that are easy to get wrong.

**It is inside the rounding.** §5.3 writes `round(q × p × f × price × (1 − d%))`, so a 50 % discount on 1.05 is round(0.525) = 0.53 half up. Rounding first and subtracting a rounded discount gives 1.05 − 0.53 = 0.52, a cent out, and every realistic test case hides the difference — this one does not.

**It does not reduce the cost.** `at-cost-aware` is sold at 500/day for 2 days with a cost of 300/day. The 20 % discount takes the net from 1 000.00 to 800.00 and leaves `cost_net` at 600.00, so the margin falls from 400.00 to 200.00 and the margin percentage from 40 % to 25 %. If the discount reduced the cost too, the margin percentage would be 40 % either way — which is the one number a producer uses to decide whether the discount is affordable. This is a DECISION and departs from the A1 prompt's literal "same formula with unit_cost"; see `engine._line_result`.
